Subject: Post-demo: Redwood fit — security preflight

Thanks for the demo earlier today — Nathan and I appreciated how the runtime handled bursty inference in the example. Before we move to a technical intake, security has a short checklist we need to start: 

- Can you confirm current SOC 2 status (Type/Scope/date)?
- Do you have a current DPA template and GDPR data processing details?
- Is HIPAA support available and what deployment modes does it cover (hosted/dedicated/private)?
- We'd like to kick off a vendor security questionnaire (standard SIG/CAIQ) and get an incident response timeline summary (expected customer notification SLA for confirmed exposures, escalation contacts).

Separately, for BCP/DR evidence we usually ask for a short excerpt of your IR playbook and a statement on log retention/forensics windows (12 months preferred). Can you point us to where those artifacts live or attach redacted copies?

Our timeline: procurement wants an intake packet by next Friday (2026-09-03). Ideally we close the security intake before scheduling a pilot. Let me know if you can share the SOC/DPA and a redacted IR playbook this week, and we can set a 30-min intake call to walk through specifics.

Thanks,
Samantha Cole
Head of Security Operations

From: markus_klein@redwood.example

Hi Samantha — great to meet you both virtually today. Quick answers and next steps below, happy to expand on a call.

SOC 2: Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II for core inference and control plane in November 2025 (scope: platform operations, delivery pipeline, customer data handling). We maintain quarterly control reviews and an annual Type II audit cadence. I'll attach a short SOC 2 summary PDF and the auditor letter.

DPA/GDPR: We have a standard DPA (v3) that includes subprocessors, SCPs for data subject requests, and roles/responsibilities. I'll attach the DPA and a short GDPR processing FAQ that explains data retention, pseudonymization, and export controls.

HIPAA: We offer HIPAA-compliant configurations for enterprise customers under an executed BAA. That typically maps to Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted API can be covered if contracted with extra controls (customer-managed keys, data routing). Procurement/legal handles the BAA templates.

Incident response / notification: our standard commitment is: initial acknowledgement of a reported security incident within 2 business hours, an initial technical assessment within 24 hours, and customer notification for confirmed data exposure within 72 hours from time of confirmation. For events that present imminent risk (e.g., active exfiltration), we provide immediate notification and a tailored remediation plan. We can provide a redacted excerpt of the IR playbook and a short timeline matrix for your intake packet.

BCP/DR & logs: retention for audit logs is configurable per account; default retention is 180 days but we support 12 months upon request (enterprise plans). We use envelope encryption; customers can bring their own keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated.

Attachments I'll send in a follow-up message: SOC2-snapshot-2025.pdf, DPA-v3.docx, and a redacted IR_playbook excerpt. If that works, can we schedule the 30-min intake on Thursday (2026-09-02) or Friday (2026-09-03)?

Best,

Thanks Mark — that timeline is helpful. Two quick clarifications before your attachments: 

1) For the "customer notification within 72 hours" point — is that from time of detection or time of confirmation? EdgeSec needs the policy to align with our internal breach program (we operate on "confirmed exposure" as the trigger).
2) For logs/forensics: does Redwood provide event-level audit logs that include request metadata, user/account identifiers, and request/response hashes needed for forensic reconstruction? If some of that is redacted in hosted by default, what's the lift to enable full auditing?
3) For HIPAA BAAs: can you confirm which deployment modes support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in HSMs? We prefer to keep key material under our control for any PHI workloads.

If you can drop the artifacts in a secure link (shared Drive or SFTP) and we can have the intake call Thursday 2026-09-02 10:00am PT. I'll pencil that in — if that's not available let me know alternatives.

— Samantha

Hi Samantha — looping in a few specifics and the attachments (redacted) for your intake packet. Attached: IR_playbook-redacted.pdf, SOC2-snapshot-2025.pdf, Retention-and-logs-summary.txt. I've also uploaded the DPA-v3.docx to the secure folder — link below.

Clarifications: 
- The 72-hour customer notification window is counted from time of confirmation of exposure. We will provide an initial acknowledgement and assessment earlier (as Mark noted).
- Hosted API: we collect request metadata and high-level request/response hashes by default; full request/response capture (forensic-grade) can be enabled for Dedicated and Private deployments or as a configurable option for Hosted under a contract amendment. Enabling full auditing typically requires a config change plus storage/retention adjustments — we can scope that in the intake.
- CMKs/HSM: Customer-managed key support is available for Dedicated and Private; hosted-api customers can use a managed KMS option but not BYOK in the shared-tenant path. For BAAs we require CMK or Dedicated/Private to satisfy key segregation requirements for PHI.

2) 30-min intake call to walk the IR timeline, audit logs, and any BAA questions (proposed: Thu 2026-09-02 10:00am PT).

4) If an expedited forensic run is needed, we'll propose an MSA addendum and an evidence transfer plan (SFTP/secure vault).
